process_type: Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) and Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD)
summary: The study investigates the fabrication and performance of ultrathin yttrium-doped barium zirconate (BYZ) membranes as electrolytes for intermediate-temperature protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) using atomic layer deposition (ALD) and pulsed laser deposition (PLD). The ALD process achieved a maximum power density of 136 mW/cm² at 400 /C176C, outperforming PLD membranes. The performance difference is attributed to surface morphology and interfacial microstructure.
evidence: The membranes were fabricated by both atomic layer deposition (ALD) and pulsed laser deposition (PLD) techniques on micromachined Si substrates. The best-performing cell demonstrated 136 mW/cm² at 400 /C176C employing a BYZ membrane fabricated by ALD and 120 mW/cm² at 450 /C176C employing a BYZ fabricated by PLD.
